newsitem.title: UK: Johnston Group off 19 pct on profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Johnston Group off 19 pct on profits warning.

text.p: British building materials and engineering company Johnston Group Plc fell 19 percent, or 85 pence, to 365 pence a share on Friday after it issued a profits warning.
The group said in a statement its results for the six months to June 30, 1997, would be below the level of last year because of difficult trading conditions in two of its three divisions.
While the second half usually accounts for most of the annual profits, it was unlikely to compensate sufficiently for the "disappointments" in the first half.

"Accordingly the board believes that the current market expectations for an increase in full-year profits will not be met and the profit may not match the outcome of last year," the company said in a statement.
It said a further trading update would be given with the interim results in October.

The group said its UK engineering business was suffering from the strength of sterling and would show a reduction in profit for the first half. Also, losses in its U.S. sweeper business grew "considerably" in the half, mainly as a result of manufacturing difficulties in introducing a new cab.

In contracting and construction, its surfacing company was affected by the poor weather in June -- traditionally one of its most profitable months -- and would make a loss in the first half. Slower anticipated progress in claims negotiations would result in the construction company making a loss, it added.
The performance of the construction materials division, however, has been "well ahead of the comparable period last year".
